Title:
LoopBridge: Should Prefill and Decode Loop Equally?

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
34 pages, 17 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/loopbridge

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models reuse one layer block for the same number of loops during prefill and decode, despite asymmetric serving costs: on batch-1 chain-of-thought tasks, prefill takes under 3% of wall time while decoding takes over 97%. We ask whether prefill and decode should loop equally, and find they should not: reading prompts with more loops (m) and decoding with fewer (n < m) shifts the frontier across Thinking Machines' 26.4B sparse-MoE Inkling-2 models (TML-d24-varloop, Inkling-2-Mini; 1M context in Day-0 vLLM) and dense 1.4B-2.6B Ouro backbones, revealing a two-regime law. On variable-depth 26.4B MoEs at n >= 2 (60,256 four-sample rollouts across 14 five-benchmark arms), training-free untying works natively, and 0.017-0.025%-parameter prompt KV-only maps (r = 0, zero decode overhead) lift 4/2 by +2.8 points (+4.3 on 256K-1M tasks, +9.5 on 512K MRCR, +2.0 on 1M LongBench v2) over 2/2 at 1.75x decode speed vs. 4/4 while 4/3 recovers 99.0% of 4/4 (74.1 vs. 74.9) at 1.27x-1.29x speed; a 2x2 causal control proves +2.7 (p < 10^-3) over matched-data KV-only 2/2, with zero-synthetic 4/2 still winning by +1.7. On fixed-depth backbones or n = 1, naive untying collapses; our LoopBridge adapter (0.13-0.25% on 26.4B MoEs; 2.4% on Ouro-2.6B) folds prompt KV maps once at prefill with merged decode LoRA, sweeping tied distillation 5/5 on 26.4B MoEs (+5.1 on Inkling-2-Mini 3/2, rescuing a 2.2% collapse; +7.8 on TML-varloop 3/1), lifting Ouro-2.6B 4/1 from 44.2 to 58.2 (vs. 49.5 distilled), and matching Ouro-2.6B-Thinking 4/4 on GSM8K at 2.0x throughput. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/loopbridge
